source.title: VILA: On Pre-training for Visual Language Models
source.authors: Ji Lin; Hongxu Yin; Wei Ping; Yao Lu; Pavlo Molchanov; A. Tao; Hui-Zi Mao; Jan Kautz; M. Shoeybi; Song Han

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies visual-language pretraining choices, not scaling laws. It mentions scaling language-model size and training corpus in related work and cites Hoffmann et al., but does not test or rely on the claimed loss laws.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a training-loss comparison between MMC4 and MMC4-pairs (Figure 5), but does not vary model parameters, training tokens, or compute to fit or test a scaling law. Its downstream benchmark results and architecture/pretraining ablations do not test the claim versions. The loss comparison is recorded as a related finding, not as evidence for a version.
record.test_reason: VILA studies visual-language pretraining design choices (freezing vs updating the LLM, interleaved vs paired data, joint SFT). It fits no power law, sweeps no parameters, tokens or compute, and makes no extrapolation or allocation claim. It cites Hoffmann et al. only in related work, on LLMs gaining capability by scaling. The 7B vs 13B comparison (Table 5, Table 6) is a two-point model-size comparison of benchmark scores. It is not a test of predictable downstream scaling (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that updating the LLM during pretraining, using interleaved image-text data, and re-blending text-only instruction data in SFT improve VLMs. They draw no scaling-law conclusions.
record.recipe_differences: Visual-language pretraining ablations and benchmark evaluations, rather than a language-model scaling-law sweep or fit.
record.method_sensitivity: Training loss differs between MMC4 and MMC4-pairs; the paper attributes the lower MMC4 loss to the additional text segments in the interleaved samples.

fits_no_version.finding: Interleaved MMC4 pretraining gives lower training loss than MMC4-pairs (Figure 5). The authors attribute this to the full text segments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLM pretraining, interleaved image-text data yields lower training loss than the same data split into image-text pairs.

record.problems: The training-loss comparison is shown as a plot without stated numerical values or uncertainty. The paper does not provide scaling-law sweeps or fits relevant to the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on the claim versions. The downstream benchmark results, text-only capability evaluations, and other pretraining ablations are not scaling-law tests.

untested.parts: No sweep or power-law fit of loss over parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count. Projector type and resolution ablations concern downstream accuracy, not loss shape-invariance.
Multimodal training is studied, but no power-law form is tested across scale.
Only two LLM sizes (7B, 13B) are compared on benchmarks. No predictability or loss-to-task relation is tested.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices are examined.

record.verdict_notes: The 'Scaling up VLM pre-training' section (4.1) describes engineering choices: higher resolution, a 13B backbone, and 50M images. It contains no scaling-law analysis, so the 7B vs 13B results were reasonably left out.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from smaller runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count bearing on loss scaling.
The paper studies visual-language pretraining, but does not test whether its loss follows a power law across scale or training regimes.
Downstream benchmarks are reported, but the paper does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted exponents, fitting choices, or bends in scaling curves.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss for pre-training on interleaved MMC4 data versus MMC4-pairs.
rows.value: MMC4 training loss is lower than MMC4-pairs training loss.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes MMC4's loss as lower, but the plotted loss comparison does not establish a power-law relationship. The figure gives no textual numeric values. The model and its size are not stated for this figure.
rows.check: Training-loss comparison between data formats (MMC4 vs MMC4-pairs) at a presumed fixed Llama-2 7B (the default ablation backbone). It does not vary scale, so it bears on no version. Subject could be stated as Llama-2 7B-based VLM per Section 4.1. No numeric values are given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
